channel.title: DETAIL Magazine
channel.description: Nejnovější architektonické projekty a články z Detail.de

item.title: Building or Sculpture?
item.description: In the heart of Munich’s Maxvorstadt district, Kéré Architecture and HK Architekten have built an oasis for children at the Technical University of Munich. The freestanding timber structure was approved because it has been classified as a sculpture.

item.title: DETAIL Facade Congress 2026
item.description: The Detail Facade Congress on 21 May 2026 will demonstrate that facades are more than just attractive outer shells; they are adaptive and climate-friendly building envelopes.

item.title: Spaziu Davia Franceschini in Corsica by A Fabrica Architettura
item.description: For a long time, an undeveloped plot of land lay next to Corbara Church. The new village square with its community centre not only blends in perfectly with the local topography – its retaining walls and facades were also constructed using earth excavated from the building site.

item.title: Superhuman Principles
item.description: Architecture has always been obsessed with nature – equally with nature as a model, its representation, and the distinction between architecture and nature. In the rich programme of the World Congress of Architecture (UIA) in Barcelona, current perspectives on this theme were expressed incidentally through the buildings and processes presented.

item.title: Casa CLO in Tarragona by Alventosa Morell Arquitectes
item.description: With their tiered timber structure clad in corrugated sheet metal, Alventosa Morell Arquitectes has created a peaceful retreat amidst a pine forest with sweeping views of the sea.

item.title: “Rammed Earth Needs Good Boots and a Good Hat”
item.description: Jonathan Tuckey has built a house out of rammed earth in Wiltshire, in the south of England. In the interview, he talks about his motivations and the particular challenges of building with earth.

item.title: A Rammed Earth House in Wiltshire
item.description: A short film portrait of the English country house built from rammed earth by Tuckey Design Studio.

item.title: Samuel H. Scripps Theater Center by Studio Gang
item.description: In Garrison, New York, Studio Gang has created the first permanent venue for the Hudson Valley Shakespeare theatre company. The Samuel H. Scripps Theater Center is a valuable addition to the entire performing arts scene.

item.title: Mäckler’s Terminal 3 – A Flight Canopy for Departures
item.description: Christoph Mäckler’s Terminal 3 is more than just a tribute to Mies van der Rohe, Martin Elsässer, and James Stirling. The ability to expand the departure hall and piers as operations continue ensures the building’s future viability.

item.title: Reflected in Friendship
item.description: Jacques Herzog and Pierre de Meuron have shaped contemporary architecture like few others, with an impressive portfolio of nearly 700 distinctive built and unbuilt projects.

item.title: Titlis Tower in Engelsberg by Herzog & de Meuron
item.description: At an elevation of over 3 000 metres above sea level, Herzog & de Meuron has transformed an antenna tower into an iconic steel sculpture. Visitors can enjoy the panoramic views of the glacier from the viewing platform and take a break in the restaurant.

item.title: „You Don’t Get That Many Penalty Kicks in a Lifetime.“
item.description: Ansgar Schulz supervised the construction of the Mother-of-Pearl Immersive Museum in Adorf, Saxony, from the very beginning. In our interview he describes which challenges the realisation of the hypar shell entailed and why rain played a central role in addressing them.

item.title: Goiáns Community Centre in Galicia by Nula.Studio
item.description: In the sprawling village of Goiáns, the team at Nula.Studio has created a bright-red community centre with a roof featuring numerous folds, thereby establishing a landmark that symbolises community spirit.

item.title: Renovation of the Caffè Nazionale in Arzignano
item.description: The architectural practice AMAA has restored the historic Caffè Nazionale in Arzignano, in northern Italy. The design combines the existing building fabric with new elements to create a spatial sequence linking the interior and exterior spaces.

item.title: Hair Salon as Sound Laboratory
item.description: With the Salt Salon, London-based studio Unknown Works combines architecture, club culture and digital fabrication to demonstrate how the interplay of precision, materials and improvisation can create an entirely new spatial experience.

item.title: Light from a single component
item.description: The Somnium lighting system from Artemide combines the lens, anti-glare shield and housing into a single component, achieving a UGR of less than 16. This is a design approach that rethinks the norm.

item.title: Studioninedots Creates Spaces for a New Way of Living Together
item.description: In Amsterdam, Studioninedots has designed a residential building comprising stacked room modules. Interstitial spaces, glass blocks and a lightweight structure create flexible living environments.

item.title: Hotel Leo in St. Gallen by Boltshauser Architects
item.description: The Hotel Leo in the garden of the Villa Wiesental is clad in greenish and white-grey clinker brick. The interior walls are made of clay bricks and earth blocks.

item.title: House 14a in Copenhagen by Pihlmann Architects
item.description: From the outside, the house from the 1950s has changed very little. Inside, Pihlmann Architects and art historian Marianne Krogh have created open, flowing spaces.

item.title: Performing Arts Centre in Brighton by krft
item.description: For the Performing Arts Centre at Brighton College, Krft and Nicholas Hare Architects designed a solitaire with a shell of flint blocks and light grey Seeton bricks.

item.title: Student-Built Observatory near Barcelona
item.description: The Flora observatory built near Barcelona for observing nature was developed and erected by a team of students and researchers at the Institute for Advanced Architecture of Catalonia.

item.title: Creative Solutions to Combat the Climate Crisis
item.description: British architect Sarah Wigglesworth drew international attention with her Straw Bale House in London. In this interview with Heide Wessely, she describes how to design cities more sustainably.

item.title: London’s Tallest Circular-Design Office Building Made of Wood
item.description: With the Black & White Building, Waugh Thistleton have not only created London’s tallest solid-wood office building, but have also made a significant contribution to the circular economy.

item.title: Wilkinson Eyre Overhaul Battersea Power Station in London
item.description: On behalf of an investor from Malaysia, Wilkinson Eyre have transformed London’s Battersea Power Station into a shopping mall featuring offices and flats. For the most part, the interiors of the impressive turbine halls have been preserved.

item.title: The Mercury Store in New York by CO Adaptive Architecture
item.description: Assigned the task of repurposing an industrial building into a performing arts centre, the architects consistently set their focus on retaining and opening its historical structure.

item.title: The Plato Art Gallery in the Czech Republic by KWK Promes
item.description: In the Czech city of Ostrava, KWK Promes have transformed an old slaughterhouse into an art gallery. The dilapidated condition of the exposed-brick building represented both challenge and inspiration for the planners.

item.title: Museum of Art and Photography by Mathew & Ghosh Architects
item.description: In the Indian metropolis of Bangalore, architects Mathew & Ghosh have realized the Museum of Art and Photography. Collections of South Asian art and culture have been displayed here since the middle of February.

item.title: The Rambla Climate House in Spain
item.description: In a suburb of the Spanish city of Molina de Segura, Andrés Jaque and his office Offpolinn have created the Rambla Climate House, a single-family dwelling conceived as a climate- and eco-house. The project won the 2022 Simon Architecture Prize.

item.title: Where’s the Journey Headed? – Editorial Detail 3.2023
item.description: The current issue of Detail takes a look at new beginnings. Few sectors of the economy were so battered during the corona years as the hotel industry.

item.title: Frame House in California
item.description: Mork-Ulnes are designing a single-family house that will withstand future disasters.

item.title: Modular House in Madrid
item.description: The DelaVegaCanolasso architecture studio specialize in small houses using modular techniques. In this video, Ignacio de la Vega and Pilar Cano-Lasso shed light on their latest project, the Fresnos house in Madrid.

item.title: Sensors for connected lighting control
item.description: Trilux is expanding its range of lighting management systems to include sensor technology for energy-efficient lighting concepts with IntuSens. The system comprises five product ranges and can be used to plan lighting solutions for a variety of settings, from offices and educational buildings to industrial premises.

item.title: Sports field, heavy rain and a building component
item.description: Heavy rainfall presents a unique challenge for paved sports surfaces. Hauraton’s Sportfix system integrates drainage and water treatment within the channel itself, eliminating the need for external filters.

item.title: Wood instead of ceramics
item.description: Agape presents its first collaboration with David Chipperfield Architects: the Tambre, a wooden bathtub that reimagines classic bathroom designs.
